about: Deterministic temporal cases for M16. One file, two consumers: tests/test_temporal_m16.py and tools/temporal_check.mjs. Both must produce the expectations recorded here, so the Python analysis tool and the browser module cannot drift apart. Scores are the stored heuristic-v1 scores; nothing here is live data.

rules.note: trend needs at least min_samples valid samples spanning at least min_duration_seconds; the least-squares slope of score against elapsed hours is STEADY inside +/- slope_tolerance_per_hour, otherwise RISING or FALLING. An interval is a gap when it exceeds max(gap_median_multiplier * median interval, gap_floor_seconds).

cases.name: empty
cases.why: no rows at all must not crash and must not invent a trend

cases.name: one_sample
cases.why: a single row has a score but no change to describe

cases.name: two_samples
cases.why: two rows give a net change but still no direction

cases.name: flat
cases.why: identical scores are steady, not rising

cases.name: rising
cases.why: a monotonic climb inside one hour

cases.name: falling
cases.why: a monotonic decline, including out of WARNING and back to NORMAL

cases.name: noisy_flat
cases.why: scores that wobble by one point of the range are steady: the slope, not the last pair, decides

cases.name: slow_rise_above_tolerance
cases.why: 0.04 per hour is four times the tolerance and must be called RISING

cases.name: slow_rise_below_tolerance
cases.why: 0.01 per hour is inside the tolerance and must be called STEADY even though the net change is positive

cases.name: duplicate_timestamp
cases.why: the later row for an identical timestamp wins, and the duplicate never becomes a zero-length interval

cases.name: out_of_order
cases.why: rows arriving unsorted are put in order before anything is measured

cases.name: invalid_rows
cases.why: missing, null, non-numeric, NaN and Infinity scores are dropped, and the newest valid row still ends the series

cases.name: out_of_range_scores
cases.why: scores below 0 or above 1 are not real heuristic-v1 output, so they are dropped rather than charted off-scale

cases.name: large_gap
cases.why: a 38 minute hole in a ten minute cadence is one gap and must qualify the trend

cases.name: no_gap_in_uneven_cadence
cases.why: a 20 minute step in a 20 minute cadence is normal cadence, not a hole

cases.name: band_crossings
cases.why: every band transition appears in the stored classes; the scores sit well clear of the engine's 0.35 / 0.6 / 0.8 edges so the expected classes cannot depend on how a boundary is rounded. This window peaks in the middle, so the least-squares slope is positive while the series ends lower than its peak: the trend field follows the slope, and the peak and net change are reported separately rather than being bent to match.

cases.name: stale_newest
cases.why: the series ends 42 minutes before now: the summary still describes it, and the caller is told the newest sample is old

incident_cases.name: open_warning
incident_cases.why: an incident the record itself calls open stays open, and its running time counts from opened_ts_epoch

incident_cases.name: warning_to_critical
incident_cases.why: the record keeps the class it opened with, so an escalation is provable and never inferred from ordinary history

incident_cases.name: resolved
incident_cases.why: a closed record with only its two timestamps still reports a duration, derived from those stamps

incident_cases.name: legacy_malformed
incident_cases.why: a record with no timestamps and no duration reports what it has and nothing more

incident_cases.name: unknown_severity
incident_cases.why: a record that states nothing must not be handed an invented severity, duration or open state
